source.title: Stacking Your Transformers: A Closer Look at Model Growth for Efficient LLM Pre-Training
source.authors: Wen-Yu Du; Tongxu Luo; Zihan Qiu; Ze-Yu Huang; Yikang Shen; Reynold Cheng; Yi-Ke Guo; Jie Fu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream benchmark performance across training scales, but its primary intervention is model growth rather than the original scaling-law measurement. Its own loss-scaling analysis uses training loss, not explicitly held-out loss.
record.gate_note: The paper fits training-loss curves against FLOPs and extrapolates those fitted curves, but does not measure held-out pretraining loss for those fits or validate the extrapolations against larger runs. Its growth-timing and growth-factor searches concern the Gstack procedure, not the standard parameter/token compute-optimal allocation in V3. The paper also reports a Samba stacking experiment, but does not fit a power law for that setting.
record.test_reason: The paper is about a model-growth method (Gstack). Every result row compares Gstack with scratch training at matched tokens or FLOPs, which is the study's own method against a baseline. Its one power-law fit (Fig. 7, L_C = aC^b on training/final loss for 410M–7B) uses the scaling-law form as a tool. It reports no coefficients and no fit quality, and it does not validate its 13B/70B 'predictions' against real runs. It therefore relies on the finding without testing any version. The downstream rows measure a Gstack-vs-scratch accuracy gap, not whether downstream performance tracks scale or loss predictably, so they do not bear on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that depthwise stacking accelerates LLM pre-training up to 7B and 750B tokens. They give empirical rules for growth timing and growth factor, and call their Gstack scaling law an initial, compute-limited estimate.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates model growth and fits its own training-loss-versus-FLOPs curves, rather than reproducing the original scaling-law sweeps or compute-optimal allocation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that growth timing and growth factor affect results: the smoothed IsoFLOP curves indicate an optimal growth timing, and the optimal growth factor is reported to lie between 2 and 4 in tested settings. It also reports different outcomes across growth directions and stacking variants.

fits_no_version.finding: Depthwise stacking (Gstack) reaches the same training loss with less compute than scratch training: about 54.6% speedup at 7B/300B tokens, and 31.0% at 700B tokens for 410M. The fitted Gstack loss-vs-FLOPs curve lies below the scratch curve.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model growth by depthwise stacking shifts the loss-compute curve, reducing compute needed to reach a given training loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Gstack models score higher on Harness average accuracy than scratch models at matched tokens (+2.1 at 3B/240B tokens; reported gains at 7B and 410M).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depthwise stacking improves downstream benchmark accuracy at a fixed training budget.

record.problems: The authors state that computation limits the scaling-law estimate and growth-factor analysis; training runs were sometimes interrupted by higher-priority tasks, leaving cosine learning-rate schedules incomplete. The paper reports no error bars or multiple-run uncertainty estimates, citing the cost of LLM pre-training.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were left out.

untested.parts: The scratch L=aC^b fit is shown only in a figure, on training loss, with no exponent or fit quality reported.
The 13B/70B extrapolations in Fig. 7 are not checked against actual runs.
No relation between downstream accuracy and scale or loss is fitted or tested.

missing.what: Scratch-baseline power-law fit of final training loss vs FLOPs across 410M–7B; figure only, no coefficients. Relevant only if a researcher wants this as a weak V1 data point.

record.verdict_notes: The record over-linked method-comparison downstream rows to V6 and gave V6 verdicts. All rows should be ['none'] and no verdicts are warranted. Train loss is used throughout; no held-out pretraining loss is reported for the fits.

versions.untested_parts: The scaling-law fit is for training/final loss against FLOPs, not explicitly held-out loss; the paper does not separately test loss against parameters or tokens with the other quantities non-bottlenecked.
The paper extrapolates fitted curves to predictions involving 13B and 70B models, but does not report those larger runs to validate predictive accuracy.
The paper searches growth timing and growth factor for Gstack, not the loss-minimising parameter and token allocation at fixed compute. It does not compare the Kaplan and Hoffmann allocation trends.

The paper compares model-growth operators and growth directions using training loss, but does not establish whether held-out loss changes only slightly across architecture shapes at fixed parameter count.
The paper does not test whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or the listed training regimes. Its Samba experiment reports stacking results, not a scaling-law fit.

The paper reports downstream benchmark performance over training scale, but does not fit or validate a quantitative predictive relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss or scale.

The paper notes resource and fitting limitations, but does not test how published scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations vary with counting, schedule, data, or fitting choices, nor whether curves depart from a power law.

rows.subject: Gstack 3B LLM
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated downstream NLP benchmark average accuracy across training compute and tokens; compared with scratch training.
rows.value: improvement of 2.1 in NLP benchmarks average accuracy
rows.note: The paper states this comparison directly; it does not provide a predictive fit for benchmark accuracy.
rows.check: This is a method comparison (Gstack 3B vs scratch 3B at 240B tokens, +2.1 avg accuracy), not a measure of downstream predictability with scale or loss. It should not be linked to V6.

rows.subject: Gstack 7B LLM
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated average accuracy on NLP benchmarks across training compute and tokens; compared with scratch training.
rows.note: The text says Gstack significantly outperforms scratch in average accuracy across NLP benchmarks; numerical accuracy values are not given in the text.
rows.check: This is a method comparison at 7B and the value is figure-only. It does not measure V6's relationship, so the 'observed' state for V6 is unfounded.

rows.subject: Gstack 410M LLM
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated average accuracy on standard NLP benchmarks across training compute and tokens; compared with scratch training.
rows.measure: Average accuracy across standard NLP benchmarks
rows.note: The main text says the evaluation results at this scale have similar findings to the reported loss improvements; the average-accuracy curve is shown without numeric values or a specific textual comparison.
rows.check: This is a method comparison at 410M and the value is figure-only. The 'partial' state has no basis against any version.

rows.subject: Gstack models (410M, 1.1B, 3B, and 7B)
rows.operation_detail: Fit loss against FLOPs using a power-law form for scratch and Gstack model results.
rows.measure: Training/final loss as a function of FLOPs
rows.value: The authors report that the Gstack fit achieves the same target loss with much less compute; numeric fitted coefficients are not stated.
rows.note: This is a reported fit for training/final loss, not explicitly held-out loss, so it does not bear on the listed held-out-loss versions.
rows.check: The power-law fit is on training/final loss vs FLOPs, with no coefficients or goodness of fit reported. The row's 'observed' value describes the Gstack-vs-scratch efficiency comparison, not a power-law test.

rows.subject: Gstack 410M LLM
rows.operation_detail: Compared training-loss curves with scratch training at high token counts and estimated the Gstack loss advantage.
rows.measure: Acceleration to the same training loss
rows.note: The paper describes the loss advantage as persisting at high token counts; this is not a held-out-loss scaling-law test.
rows.check: This is a speedup of the study's own method relative to scratch; it bears on no version.

rows.subject: Gstack 410M LLM
rows.operation_detail: Compared training-loss curves with scratch training at high token counts and estimated the Gstack loss advantage.
rows.measure: Acceleration to the same training loss
rows.note: The paper reports continued acceleration at 700B tokens; this is not a held-out-loss scaling-law test.
rows.check: This is a speedup of the study's own method relative to scratch; it bears on no version.
